 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of otor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of Chandappa in a motor vehicles accident dated 21.05.2020.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. Petitioners are the wife and children of deceased-Chandappa.

It is the case of the petitioners' that on 21.05.2020 at 10:00 a.m. the deceased was travelling as pillion rider on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-36-ES- 9323 ('motorcycle' for short) towards Jamalpur tanda.
It was ridden by petitioner No.3-Suresh.

On Narayanapur- Hunasagi road, another motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-28- EX-2930 ('offending vehicle' for short) came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result of which, accident occurred and in the said accident, he sustained injuries and died while undergoing treatment.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text:
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have filed separate written statement denying the age, occupation,
income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependent on him.
Respondent No.2 has also pleaded that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving licence and prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
7. Petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and Exs.P1 to 11 are marked.

8. On behalf of respondent No.2 one witness is examined as RW.1 and copy of insurance policy is marked as Ex.R1.
9.

Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.12,13,948/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.
10. The details of the compensation granted are as under:
Sl . Head

Amount  No. awarded  1. Loss of dependency Rs.11,43,948/-
 2. Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/-
 3. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 4. Towards funeral and Rs.15,000/-
 transportation charges
11. Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
12. During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the notional income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The compensation granted under other heads also requires enhancement and prays to allow the appeal.
13. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

14. Heard arguments and perused the records.
15.
Having

regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, Chandappa died due to the injuries sustained in the said accident has attained finality.

sentences.text: Based on the evidence placed on record, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the deceased as 50 years and multiplier 13.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal is justified in considering the income on notional basis.
Since the accident is of the year 2020, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.13,750/- p.m. instead of Rs.11,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects.

Since the deceased was in the age group of 40-50, 25% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1, (Magma's case).

sentences.text: Therefore, the (2018) 18 SCC 130 income is required to be taken at Rs.17,187/-.
Since there are three dependents, 1/3rd deducted towards his personal and living expenses is correct.

With these components, loss of dependency is Rs.17,187 x 12 x 13 x 2/3 =
17,87,448/- as against Rs.11,43,948/- granted by the Tribunal.

17. As wife and children of deceased, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., Rs.1,20,000/- under the head loss of consortium as against Rs.40,000/-
granted by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/-
each under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses (including transportation charges).
18.

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.19,37,448/- as against Rs.12,13,948/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:
Sl. Heads Amount Amount No. awarded by the awarded by  Tribunal this Court  1. Loss of dependency Rs.11,43,948/- Rs.17,87,448/-

2 . Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/- Rs.1,20,000/-
 3. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
4. Towards funeral and Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
transportation
charges

To this extent, the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.19,37,448/-
together with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rs.12,13,948/- granted by the Tribunal.

(iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order (minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
